name: Heidelberg-Moscow
summary: Heidelberg-Moscow used enriched germanium detectors at Gran Sasso for a long-running germanium-76 double-beta search. A subset of authors later claimed a signal; that interpretation was disputed and is not treated here as an established discovery.
detection_principle: High-purity germanium diodes served as source and energy detector. Low-radioactivity shielding and pulse-shape selections reduced backgrounds near the 76Ge neutrinoless-decay energy.

science_scope: A neutrinoless double-beta-decay signal would establish lepton-number violation. Converting a half-life constraint into an effective Majorana mass requires a decay mechanism and nuclear matrix elements; a null search is not a neutrino-mass measurement.

media.caption: Published summed Heidelberg-Moscow detector spectrum in the high-energy range, illustrating measured radioactive backgrounds; this is not evidence of a neutrinoless-decay discovery.
